question: Does every injected bad record turn up as a rejection, with the good ones unharmed?

checks.name: the quarantine count rose by exactly the injected count
nothing is unaccounted for: published + quarantined == vehicle entities
the valid entities in the same feed were still published
every rejection was persisted beside the payload that caused it
the null-island rejections are labelled as such, not as schema failures
every bad payload from the broker reached the quarantine table
the good events from the same run landed as rows
the exported quarantine counter rose by at least the injected count

notes: The exported counter is a lower bound, not an equality: it is cumulative across processes and the drivers here are short-lived, so a count that has not been exported yet is missing rather than wrong.
Only entities the decoder accepted in the baseline were corrupted; breaking one that was already being rejected would change no count and the experiment would pass having measured nothing.

The collector writes its rejections to the snapshot archive, not to Postgres -- it deliberately has no database (ADR-006) -- which is why the feed path is checked against the sidecar and the broker path against the table.
